topIssues.title: go: default to RPC 127.0.0.1
topIssues.author: protolambda
topIssues.body:
Services all default to binding the RPC to 0.0.0.0 currently.
It's considered better to default to 127.0.0.1 to not accidentally expose an RPC publicly, like many L1 clients do.
This may break existing configurations, so this change should be coupled to a release, and goes into many releases (op-batcher/op-propoiser/op-challenger/op-node/op-conductor to name a few).

topIssues.title: [PCD] Predict L1 addresses via dry-run
topIssues.author: 0xOneTony
topIssues.body:
The L2 genesis embeds the L1 proxy addresses for `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, `L1StandardBridge`, `L1ERC721Bridge`, `OptimismPortal`, and `SystemConfig`. Since these contracts don't exist yet when the genesis is built, their addresses must be predicted. OPCM uses `CREATE2` for every proxy, so the addresses are deterministic given the salt inputs. Add a pipeline stage that calls OPCM's `deploy()` as a non-broadcasting `eth_call` and reads the returned `ChainContracts` struct, then persists the addresses to state.   
Note: OPCM mixes `msg.sender` into the CREATE2 salt for every proxy, so the dry-run must be sent from the same key that will eventually broadcast the real deploy transaction. A dry-run from a different `from` produces different predicted addresses, and the L2 genesis built from them would be invalid.

topIssues.title: default syncmode.offset-el-safe to 12h fails for --minimal nodes
topIssues.author: Creamers158
topIssues.body:
Running op-node v1.19.0 + op-reth v2.3.1 on multiple Superchain registry chains (Zora, BOB, Mode, etc.) with `--syncmode=execution-layer` Repeatedly seeing:

```
lvl=warn msg="Failed to insert unsafe payload for EL sync"
err="temp: EL sync offset-derived head at block XXXXXXX: l2 block is missing L1 info deposit tx, block hash: 0x..."
```
The error advances block-by-block and never resolves. Switching to `--syncmode=consensus-layer` masks it.

Setting `--syncmode.offset-el-safe=0` on op-node fixes it, EL sync proceeds normally with no errors.

We were also running op-reth with `--minimal`, which keeps only ~10,064 blocks of history. The default --syncmode.offset-el-safe=12h translates to ~21,600 blocks behind tip at 2s block time — could it be that the offset-derived head is pointing to a block that has already been pruned by --minimal, causing the L1 info deposit tx to appear missing? Would make sense why `--syncmode.offset-el-safe=0` resolves it.

Assumption / hypothesis:
The 12h default seems designed to protect sequencers from marking blocks as safe before L1 confirms them within the sequencing window.
For standard RPC/replica nodes that don't produce blocks, this protection has no meaningful effect, but it does silently break EL sync when paired with any pruned node profile (--minimal, --full) where the offset points beyond the retained history window.

**Suggestion**:
Would it make sense to either document this incompatibility explicitly, or only apply the 12h default when running as a sequencer?

topPRs.title: test: reproduce #21663 NUT bundle drift via L2DevFeatureFlags version bump
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Do not merge — diagnostic experiment for the CI failures in ethereum-optimism/optimism#21663.

**What this shows:** the karst/lagoon NUT activation failures come from the **semver downgrade guard** in `L2ContractsManagerUtils.upgradeTo` (reverts `L2ContractsManager_DowngradeNotAllowed` when the installed proxy version > the version the bundle installs), combined with a test-fixture gap: **L2DevFeatureFlags is not captured in any pre-fork state file**, so the NUT activation test rebuilds it from HEAD instead of the fork era.

- Before: HEAD L2DevFeatureFlags = 1.0.0, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.0,1.0.0)=false` → pass.
- After the bump: HEAD = 1.0.1, frozen bundle installs 1.0.0 → `gt(1.0.1,1.0.0)=true` → downgrade → revert.

Commits:
1. bump L2DevFeatureFlags semver 1.0.0 → 1.0.1
2. comment-only touch to the NUT test file (contracts-only changes don't set `rust_changes_detected`, so the NUT test would be skipped — a CI gap in its own right)
3. regenerate `current-upgrade-bundle.json`
4. regenerate `semver-lock.json`
5. bump the version unit test to 1.0.1 + re-snapshot the **lagoon** bundle (karst left immutable)

Expected CI after commit 5: snapshot checks + version test green; **lagoon** NUT/interop green (bundle now installs 1.0.1, matching HEAD); **karst** NUT still red (its immutable bundle installs 1.0.0 while the test's HEAD genesis has 1.0.1). Note: `nut-provenance-verify lagoon` will fail because the lock commit is the develop merge-base, which predates the change.

topPRs.title: spike: op-script-engine (Rust/revm) as op-deployer's default script engine
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
**Spike result — CI vehicle, not for merge as-is.** Will be superseded by a reviewed landing stack (in preparation); opened as a draft so the full CI matrix runs the surfaces we couldn't run locally (op-reth-EL op-e2e suites, faultproofs, full sysgo presets).

Part of #20257 §16, tracked in #21743.

What's here (spikes 1–3, +7.5k lines over 34 commits):
- `rust/op-script-engine`: revm-40 cheatcode host (no foundry deps), UDS JSON-RPC, fork mode via lazy RPC-backed state pinned by block hash.
- op-deployer + interopgen run it **by default** (`--script-engine=go` is the only fallback path, never selected by binary availability); forked hosts included.
- Parity evidence: L2Genesis `ForgeAllocs` byte-identical across all 5 alloc modes; OPCM `RunScript*`; forked A/B against hermetic fixture + live Sepolia archive; ~2.6× faster than the Go host. Three adversarial no-shortcut audits passed (no skips, no weakened assertions, no regenerated goldens).
- CI provisioning: `rust-workspace-binaries` builds the engine (`--workspace`); `RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_SCRIPT_ENGINE` exported to every job that runs op-deployer.

topPRs.title: op-script-engine: Rust forge-script executor + Go client and parity gates
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Rust `op-script-engine` crate + Go client and byte-parity gates — the base of the op-geth-decoupling script-engine stack (epic #20257 §16). **Additive: no production code selects this engine yet.**

Stack (each stacked on the previous):
1. **this PR** — engine crate, `rustengine` client, parity gates
2. non-forked op-deployer routing + engine default (follows)
3. fork-mode routing + boundary deletion (follows)

### Contents
- **`rust/op-script-engine`** — revm-based re-implementation of the `op-chain-ops/script` EVM host: a cheatcode + console `Inspector`, prank/broadcast capture, forge-artifact loader, state dump, the OPCM `RunScript*` input/output-precompile mechanism, and an RPC-backed fork mode. Served over a UDS JSON-RPC transport (reth-ipc + jsonrpsee).
- **`op-chain-ops/script/rustengine`** — Go client plus A/B parity tests that drive both the Go host and this engine and assert **byte-identical** output: state-dump + broadcast (incl. `gasUsed`), OPCM `RunScriptSingle`/`Void`, and forked `SetDisputeGameImpl` over a hermetic recorded-RPC fixture.
- **Additive helpers** the parity path needs: `script.Precompile` snapshot reflection, `script.Host.ExportDiff`, and a `forking.AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref fix. `go-tests` provisions the workspace-built binary so the gates run in CI.

### Gates (local)
- `cargo test -p op-script-engine` — 16/16
- `cargo clippy -p op-script-engine --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean; nightly `fmt` clean
- `go test ./op-chain-ops/script/rustengine/` — parity / OPCM / forked / isolated-fork all pass
- base goldens (`TestScriptStateDump|TestScriptBroadcast`) and `./op-chain-ops/script/forking/` unchanged-green

Part of #21743

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Review batch applied
Crate hardening (all byte-parity re-validated): contained worker-thread panics (`catch_unwind`); standard precompiles `0x01..=0x0a` no longer framed/broadcast-captured (matches the Go host, which frames only bytecode-bearing targets); `tx.chain_id: None` on raw calls (matches geth's `EVM.Call`, fixes a stale-id case after `vm.chainId`); host setters record into the fork diff when forked; documented that `isolate_broadcast`'s `transaction_id` bump also re-baselines SSTORE originals (revm's cold-slot reset == geth `Finalise(true)`).

Go client hardening: stderr drain uses `bufio.Reader` (no 64KiB line-cap hang); Linux `Pdeathsig=SIGKILL` so a hard-killed test can't leak engines. Test rigor: `TestMain`→`ProvisionTestBinary` + a `REQUIRE_RUST_ENGINE` guard so the byte-parity gate can't silently skip; a targeted `AccountDiff.Copy` nil-deref regression test; non-vacuity guards on the parity subtests.

**Two flagged potential divergences investigated — both non-divergences:** the implemented cheatcode set is complete for the OPCM-routed scripts (env*/toString/parseJson/file-IO are used only by the legacy forge scripts, never routed; verified by the passing full-suite A/B gates), and the isolated-broadcast SSTORE-original re-baseline is handled by revm (source-confirmed).

**One real divergence found — access control:** enforcing Go's cheatcode access control naively breaks byte parity, because the routed deploy scripts deploy helper contracts that call cheatcodes and rely on Go's transitive auto-grant-on-deploy. Left **unenforced** (the current byte-parity-correct behavior, documented in `cheatcodes.rs`); correct enforcement needs the auto-grant replicated and is a dedicated follow-up.
